title: Analytical performances and field assessment of a multiplex Real-Time PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto in wild canids fecal samples
content:
by Graziana Da Rold, Filippo Marzoli, Federica Obber, Roberto Celva, Alessia Franzoso, Giacomo De Conti, Elisa Dalla Libera, Patrizia Danesi, Sofia Sgubin, Rudi Cassini, Erica Marchiori, Dominik Trenkwalder, Piero Bonelli, Giovanna Masala, Chiara Rossi, Heidi Christine Hauffe, Carlo Vittorio Citterio

Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato are the causative agents of alveolar and cystic echinococcosis, two important zoonoses with significant public health implications. Several diagnostic approaches are currently available for the detection of these parasites in definitive hosts, including classical parasitological methods and molecular techniques. However, conventional techniques such as intestinal scraping or copromicroscopy are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and require skilled personnel, while some molecular assays may show limited sensitivity or specificity. This study aimed at developing and assessing a real-time PCR assay using species-specific probes for the diagnosis of E. multilocularis and E. granulosus sensu stricto directly from the feces of potential definitive hosts, i.e., domestic and wild canids. The methodological assessment was performed by estimating the Limit of Detection (LoD), and specificity and the assay was applied to the analysis of fresh, field-collected canid fecal samples. Our protocol demonstrated excellent analytical performance, achieving an LoD corresponding to a single egg per reaction (from 0.10 g of feces) and a specificity of 100% for both Echinococcus species. Moreover, by relying directly on DNA extraction from fecal material and eliminating the need for sequencing through the use of specific probes, this method significantly reduced laboratory time and associated costs. The assay was successfully applied to field samples collected during surveillance activities, providing results consistent with the known biology and epidemiology of Echinococcus species in the study area.
author: Graziana Da Rold
